jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Natural Perspective
jokes.joke: I got recognized at the Grand Canyon once. A guy said, “Hey, I know you!” and for one glorious second I felt famous. Then he handed me his phone and said, “Can you take our picture?” Nothing resets your ego like standing beside a natural wonder while strangers decide you’re the most replaceable tripod in Arizona.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Regional Fame
jokes.joke: I finally got recognized in public. I was at the Grand Canyon, staring into a two-mile drop, and a guy goes, "Hey, aren't you the guy from the DMV?" I said, "No." He said, "Yeah, you are. You were rude." I've never worked at a DMV. But I'll tell you, standing at the edge of a canyon, I thought about it for a second.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Grocery Store Reunion
jokes.joke: I used to be a corrections officer, and let me tell you, being recognized in public is a nightmare. I’m just trying to buy cereal with my wife, and some guy across the grocery aisle yells, 'Hey! You’re the guy who watches me pee!' Try explaining that dynamic to a cashier while holding a family-size box of Frosted Flakes.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Prison with a View
jokes.joke: I worked as a corrections officer at a prison on the rim of a canyon. Best security feature wasn’t the fences or the dogs. It was the view. Inmates would peer over the edge, see that endless drop, and suddenly decide the food wasn’t so bad. One new guy asked how we stopped escapes. I told him, Easy. We just let gravity do the correcting.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Echo Fan Club
jokes.joke: I knew I wasn’t famous, but I got way too excited at a canyon. I shouted, “Hello!” and a voice shouted it right back. For five straight minutes I thought I’d finally been recognized by a fan. Then I yelled, “You’re the best!” and the fan waited for me to say it first.

scores.comment: Strong escalation from mistaken recognition to a dark canyon-edge implication. Clean timing and a final beat that lets the audience complete the joke.
Clear, stage-ready premise with a funny public-context reveal. The Frosted Flakes tag adds texture, though the central embarrassment joke is fairly expected.
Competent setup and readable construction, but the prison-on-a-canyon premise feels engineered for the seed terms and 'gravity do the correcting' is a predictable pun.
The echo-as-fan misunderstanding is simple and accessible, with a good final reversal. Amusing, but the echo premise is familiar enough to limit surprise.
Clean stage premise and a believable turn from fame to tripod. 'Most replaceable tripod in Arizona' carries the final laugh, but the 'recognized, then asked for a photo' twist is a familiar route.

Funny, concrete image of a former guard recognized by an inmate in a grocery aisle. The final beat about the cashier and the Frosted Flakes box softens the punch a little, and the seed terms are used naturally.

Decent premise and a pun-based button ('let gravity do the correcting'). The pun lands as a groaner, and the 'inmates decide the food isn't so bad' line is the stronger beat but sits mid-joke, not at the end.
The echo gag is familiar, and the final line is a touch ambiguous because the echo can't pre-empt the speaker. The self-deflating premise works, but the payoff is mild and the logic muddy.
The mistaken-for-a-photographer trope is very familiar, but 'replaceable tripod in Arizona' provides a solid, well-crafted save at the end.
Excellent pacing and a genuinely funny dark turn. The absurd DMV accusation perfectly sets up the edge-of-the-canyon intrusive thought.
The premise feels heavily contrived simply to force the seed words together, resulting in a predictable, groan-inducing pun.
An old, simplistic echo joke. It lacks the sophistication of a stand-up act and telegraphs the punchline immediately.
Clean tourist-spot recognition setup with a solid final image; mild smile, not a strong snap.
DMV misidentification plus the canyon-edge hesitation gives a decent dark turn, but the payoff stays modest.
Specific, awkward public recognition tied to the job lands with clear stage timing and a concrete closer.
Echo-as-fan is the most obvious canyon route; the call-and-response twist feels mild and familiar.
Clear premise, efficient build, and a relatable ego-deflation turn. The tripod comparison lands, though the recognition fake-out is a familiar route.
Strong escalation from mistaken identity to unexpected accusation. The canyon context supports the dark final thought, which gives the joke its snap.
Specific perspective, vivid reveal, and a strong quoted line. The cereal and cashier tag adds texture and keeps the scene grounded.
Competent and coherent, but the gravity/correcting punchline is predictable and closer to a wordplay-based tag than a strong stand-up turn.
